# Issue #112: pointers to keys containing "~" or "/" do not resolve

Given `doc = {"~1": "tilde-one", "a/b": "slash"}`, `resolve(doc, "/~01")` raises `KeyError`,
although `"~01"` is the RFC 6901 encoding of the key `"~1"`. Keys that contain a slash
(`"/a~1b"`) are also affected in some combinations. Plain keys and list indexes work fine.

tests/test_resolve.py

arguments.summary: Fixed the RFC 6901 escape-decoding order in `pointer/resolve.py`'s `_decode()`: it previously did `token.replace("~0", "~").replace("~1", "/")`, which wrongly turned `~01` into `~1` and then into `/`, so keys like `"~1"` (encoded `/~01`) and combinations with `/`-containing keys failed to resolve. Swapped the order to `token.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~")` so escapes decode left-to-right as the RFC requires (`~01` → `~1`, never `/`). Verified with the issue's examples (`/~01` → `"tilde-one"`, `/a~1b` → `"slash"`) plus edge cases (`~0b`, `~01b`, `/~1`, `/~0`, nested pointers), and the existing test suite passes.
